summary: The simulation code is syntactically correct, imports are appropriate, and it implements the required agent-based simulation, calibration, evaluation, and JSON output. Error handling and performance safeguards (FAST_MODE, SKIP_IO) are present. Main is correctly invoked at global scope. Only minor issues were found regarding configurability, logging, and a slight deviation from the 'no global state mutation' note in module docstrings.

issues.description: get_calibrator forwards kwargs from an optional config file to calibrator constructors, but the calibrator classes do not accept any __init__ arguments. If a config file is ever provided with keys, this would raise a TypeError.
issues.solution: Either ensure calibrator __init__ signatures accept **kwargs or do not pass kwargs when instantiating calibrators. For safety, change to CALIBRATOR_REGISTRY[name]() unless constructors are updated.

issues.description: ParamsAdapter.validate_frozen returns a dict of warnings but apply() prints only the keys, not the messages. This may reduce clarity of warnings.
issues.solution: Iterate items and print both key and message, e.g., for k, msg in frozen_warnings.items(): print(f"[ParamsAdapter] Warning: {msg}", file=sys.stderr).

issues.description: Module forward docstrings say 'No global state mutation', but PolicyBroadcast and InfluenceAndAdoption mutate agent state (awareness, trust_policy, fatigue). This is inconsistent with the stated design.
issues.solution: Update docstrings to reflect intentional agent state updates or refactor to write intended changes into buffers and apply them centrally, similar to adoption updates.

issues.description: FAST_MODE defaults to enabled due to environment default ('1'), forcing reduced population and skipped I/O even when not explicitly requested.
issues.solution: Consider defaulting FAST_MODE to '0' and enabling it explicitly via CLI or environment when needed, if full-fidelity runs are desired by default.
